shouldFix.title: basedOn.d086.role asserts that D-086 named DR-G30 as required-now via gate-harness-naming. D-086 recorded gate-harness-naming.v3, whose bytes contain no occurrence of 'G30' at all, and the G30 lineage has expressly and repeatedly recorded the opposite.
shouldFix.quotedBytes: basedOn.d086 = {"recording": "D-086", "commit": "14865abc42c13b9759f5761c2873db03b708ea32", "role": "Named DR-G30 as required-now via gate-harness-naming. g30-fixture-corpus.v1 does not unwrite that naming."}
shouldFix.why: Four independent live sources refute the proposition. (1) gate-harness-naming.v3.json - the artifact D-086 records - contains zero occurrences of the substring 'G30' or 'DR-G30'; so do v1, v2, v4, v5 and v6. Only v7 and v8 contain 'DR-G30' (6 each), and neither v7 nor v8 is recorded anywhere in COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md. (2) D-086's own text fixes the scope: 'Required-now set is 18; presently recordable names are 16. G03/G04 remain required and unnamed. G17 is dropped. G13 is reserved behind DR-118.' It is dated 2026-08-14. DR-G30 was created two days later by D-158, whose heading is literally 'Add DR-G30 as required-now preview-boundary install-shape obligation' (2026-08-16), and whose commit 0fcf3d3 is subject-lined 'D-158: add DR-G30 required-now install-shape'. D-086 could not have named a row that did not yet exist. (3) File 08 - which this subject pins at file08Pin and which recomputes to the pinned e503b75b... - resolves the attribution per gate in its condition-4 row: 'G30 named under D-158'. D-086 appears only in that row's collective parenthesis of thirteen decisions that together built the naming half; the per-gate attribution immediately following it names D-158. (4) The G30 lineage has recorded the denial in terms. D-255 - the decision this same subject pins at basedOn.d255 - states verbatim: 'Naming parent is D-158, not leftover-join.v4. naming v6 does not name G30.' Occupancy v2, pinned at basedOn.occupancyV2, carries the same denial at basedOn.namingV6.role: gate-harness-naming.v6 'Does not name DR-G30.'
shouldFix.regressionNotCarry: This is authored text, not carried text. The shape comes from g21-fixture-corpus.v1 (the subject's own declared first-authoring precedent at basedOn.g21FixtureCorpusV1), whose basedOn.d086.role reads 'Named DR-G21 as required-now. This corpus does not unwrite that naming.' - and which is TRUE: gate-harness-naming.v3 contains 'DR-G21' six times and v6 contains it eight times, and g21-fixture-corpus.v1 correctly pairs it with a separate basedOn.d145 entry labelled 'Naming parent'. The g30 subject copied the entry, dropped the d145 companion (correctly, since v6 does not name G30), and ADDED the four words 'via gate-harness-naming' - which are the false part and which have no counterpart in the precedent. Byte-checking the per-gate naming parent is exactly the D-285 defect class (a drafted 'D-086 named DR-G12, G21, or G32' that was false for G32 alone).
shouldFix.selfInflicted: The subject already carries the correct attribution twice. basedOn.d158.role says 'Named DR-G30 as required-now.' and parentReview.role says 'Naming parent is D-158, not leftover-join.v4.' The d086 entry therefore does not fill a gap; it duplicates a claim that is already correctly made and attaches it to a second, wrong decision, leaving the artifact asserting two different naming acts for one row.
shouldFix.gradedShouldFix: Graded SHOULD-FIX, not MUST-FIX, on the CLAUDE-DCLJ-V8-SF1 precedent for an unverified lineage-custody claim in a role field, and under the CLAUDE-CMLJ-V12-A1 operative-force test. Nothing operative turns on it: the entry's only active clause is the disclaimer 'does not unwrite that naming', the subject binds NOTHING, adds no DR-G* row, changes no required-now count, and edits no cell; and the true attribution is independently bound at basedOn.d158.role, at parentReview.role, and in the pinned file 08 itself. It is nonetheless a false proposition about a recorded decision, sitting in the field whose whole job is to state what each cited input did - and a recorder drafting a D-000 entry from this artifact could recite 'D-086 named DR-G30' into COORD, where the register says otherwise.
shouldFix.repairShape: Delete basedOn.d086 outright, or rewrite its role to what is byte-true of D-086 with respect to this gate - that D-086 recorded gate-harness-naming.v3 as the condition-4 naming candidate at a required-now set of 18, that gate-harness-naming through v6 does not name DR-G30, and that DR-G30's naming parent is D-158. No other field of the subject needs to move: no fixture byte, no digest, no coverage mapping, and no leftoverDesign value is affected by the repair.
shouldFix.notTheDispatchTokenAttack: This is not the dispatch's bare-version-token attack, which I refute separately below. It is a false custody proposition, not an ambiguous token.
